newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO PROLONG THE AGONY OF TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO PROLONG THE AGONY OF TRIUMPH.

text.p: Monaco remain on the verge of winning their sixth French first division championship after their 1-1 draw at home against Marseille left them still short of the last crucial points needed to wrap up the title.
The team from the principality, the best in the French league, have drawn out their chase for a trophy this season to the point of agony.

That agony has taken its toll on a talented squad, who should have reached the UEFA Cup final instead of Internazionale of Italy but gave the tie away in a poor opening first 45 minutes of the away leg when they conceded three goals.

Striker Victor Ikpeba's unhappiness at almost always starting on the bench came to the boil after the match in Milan and the squad struggled to hide internal rifts as they prepared to face Marseille at home on Saturday.
The draw merely prolonged the agony of waiting to celebrate Monaco's first league title since 1988, when they were under Arsene Wenger, now manager of English premier league side Arsenal.

"After the difficult match against Inter Milan, we had to react and going behind was not the best way," coach Jean Tigana said after Sylvain Legwinski had equalised following Xavier Gravelaine's opening goal for Marseille.
"Now we must win at Strasbourg on Wednesday or against Caen (next weekend). We have our fate in our hands."

Monaco manager Henri Biancheri said: "The defeat against Inter was a huge disappointment felt by all and when we had to get back in the bath after that, we showed the effects on our morale and physical condition."
Ever since Monaco took over at the top of the first division from Paris St Germain and set about building a wide lead, other setbacks have taken the gloss off their often superb performances.

They were bundled out of the French Cup by second division Laval in the first round, a match they probably regarded as unimportant at the time as they prepared to face PSG at home in their crucial top-of-the-table clash in late January.

In February it was the League Cup, when Monaco crashed out 2-1 away to Strasbourg in the semifinals, prompting veteran defender Patrick Blondeau to criticise Tigana's attitude to another apparently less important match.
"The players were keen to play in a final and we threw this one away with bad choices," he said.
Tigana rested several key first team players and only brought on Brazilian striker Anderson and Nigeria's Ikpeba in the second half.

Marseille's performance in their first match at Monaco since early in the 1993/4 season, before their enforced relegation over the Valenciennes match-rigging scandal, confirmed their failure to improve significantly their 1996 promotion side.
"Overall, the draw was deserved," coach Gerard Gili said. "We managed to repeat some of our away performances.
"And it's the paradox of the season, to have taken four points out of six against Monaco, the virtual champions, and (only) two points against other teams less well placed."
In fact, Marseille now have only two opportunities left to avoid ending the season without an away victory when they travel to Lens next Saturday and Lyon on the last day of the season on May 24.

Their president Robert Louis-Dreyfus has pledged to strengthen the squad, saying he will have failed if they finish lower than fifth next season, and Bordeaux's brilliant coach Rolland Courbis looks set to take over from Gili.
